claims.head: Don’t buy Kuemper’s record against the Islanders
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Kuemper has been a wall against the Islanders, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Islanders finally get to him.

claims.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
claims.body: The Islanders’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Kings’ not so much. The Islanders are the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Los Angeles is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. Watch the Islanders’ defensemen jump into the play.

LAK.head: Advantage, the Kings
LAK.body: Even though Los Angeles will be without Fiala, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, the Islanders will be without Barzal. The Islanders can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

NYI.head: The Islanders face a real test
NYI.body: Even though Los Angeles will be without Fiala, the Kings have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, the Islanders will be without Barzal. The Islanders’ best way through is piling up shots.

story.head: Active D vs. Forward-led
paras: The Kings won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-2 in overtime on Long Island on Oct 22. The Islanders (7-6-2) lost 5-3 to Carolina on Nov 5, while the Kings (5-7-2) beat San Jose 7-2 on Nov 4. Going in, the Islanders are fifth in the Metropolitan (tied for 21st in the NHL) and the Kings seventh in the Pacific (tied for 28th).

The Islanders’ record (.533) is about what their chances are worth. The Kings have played better than their record (.429) says: their chances are worth about .613, mostly because they’re 2-5 in one-goal games.

The Islanders get their defensemen shooting (1st), roll their lines more evenly than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (2nd). The Kings, by contrast, lean hard on their top players (4th lowest). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd). They also leave the shooting to their forwards (lowest), so the Isles’ defensemen shoot a lot, and theirs not so much. The Kings’ forecheck could keep the Islanders pinned in their own end.

Matthew Schaefer (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 15 GP) leads the Islanders in scoring, and Bo Horvat (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 15 GP) has a team-high seven goals. For the Kings, Artemi Panarin (8 G / 9 A / 17 P in 14 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and ten goals in 13 games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Adrian Kempe (6 G / 6 A / 12 P in 13 GP) is next in line.

Ilya Sorokin (6-4-0 / .911 SV% in 10 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and will likely start. Darcy Kuemper (5-3-1 / .885 SV% in 9 GS) is in line to start for Los Angeles. Kuemper has a .933 save percentage in seven starts against the Islanders, well above his usual .900. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

items.text: The Islanders are newly without Ryan Pulock, have been without Matias Maccelli since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Mathew Barzal all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Mammoth and the Ducks are missing more right now.
The Kings have been without Alex Turcotte and Mats Zuccarello for several games, and have had to make do without Kevin Fiala all season.
Alex Laferriere has two goals on chances worth about 6.5 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Ilya Sorokin has never won in Los Angeles: he is 0-4-0 there in his career.
